review:
SUMMARY: 7 confirmed bugs identified across connection pooling, HA routing, validation, and SQL AST modules. Issues include contract violations, race conditions, permanent state mutation, NPEs, and broken collection semantics.

POINTS:
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/DruidDataSource.java:283] tryGetConnection() violates non-blocking contract; TOCTOU race allows getConnection() to block up to maxWait — fix: return getConnection(0);
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/ha/selector/RandomDataSourceSelector.java:206] removeBlackList() returns all data sources including blacklisted ones when blacklist threshold is met, bypassing the blacklist — fix: properly filter out blacklisted sources instead of short-circuiting to all
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/ha/selector/RandomDataSourceValidateThread.java:201] Non-atomic errorCounts increment loses updates under concurrency, delaying or preventing blacklist decisions — fix: replace non-atomic get/put with atomic compute or AtomicInteger
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/DruidPooledConnection.java:253] Single cross-thread close permanently sets async close flag on shared datasource, degrading performance for all subsequent connections — fix: remove permanent flag mutation on shared datasource
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/xa/JtdsXAResource.java:90] isSameRM() throws NPE when getRmHost() returns null due to failed reflection initialization — fix: add null check before calling .equals()
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/sql/ast/SQLJSONValueExpr.java:10] equals() always returns false and hashCode() always returns 0, violating Object contract and breaking HashMap/HashSet semantics — fix: implement proper equals/hashCode with identity and field checks
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/druid/pool/ha/selector/RandomDataSourceSelector.java:226] Guard prevents removing all busy data sources when they equal the total, causing routing to sources with zero available connections — fix: adjust guard to allow removing all busy sources or return empty set

suspicions.observation: In PreparedStatementPool.LRUCache.removeEldestEntry (line 192-199), when the eldest entry is removed due to size limit, closeRemovedStatement(eldest.getValue()) is called. But closeRemovedStatement at line 163 checks `if (holder.isInUse()) { return; }` and returns early without closing. This means in-use statements get removed from the LRU cache map but are NOT closed, and since they're removed from the map, they won't be re-added when returned. The in-use statement will have nowhere to go when its user is done with it - it leaks because it was evicted from the pool but not tracked.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Evicted PreparedStatement that is still in use is removed from the LRU cache but never closed and never returned to the pool, causing a resource leak

suspicions.observation: In DruidDataSource.getConnection(String username, String password) at line 2290-2309, the first branch (lines 2291-2298) directly assigns `this.username = username` and `this.password = password` without any locking. Since these fields are shared state and `username`/`password` are also volatile (from DruidAbstractDataSource), concurrent calls with different credentials could cause a race where one thread gets a connection with credentials mixed from different calls. Additionally, after setting these credentials, there's no revalidation that the existing pooled connections use the new credentials.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Race condition in getConnection(username, password) - concurrent calls can corrupt username/password credentials and connections may use stale credentials

suspicions.observation: In DruidDataSource.tryGetConnection() at line 283-287, it checks `if (poolingCount == 0) return null;` then calls `return getConnection();`. The `getConnection()` method can block (up to maxWait milliseconds) waiting for connections. The TOCTOU race: between checking poolingCount==0 and calling getConnection(), another thread might have taken the last pooled connection, causing this method to block indefinitely (up to maxWait) when the caller expects a non-blocking behavior.
suspicions.suspected_bug: tryGetConnection() violates its non-blocking contract - it can block even when poolingCount was 0, because getConnection() will create new connections or wait for existing ones

suspicions.observation: In DruidPooledConnection.close() at line 253, when the closing thread differs from the owner thread, `dataSource.setAsyncCloseConnectionEnable(true)` is called. This permanently sets a boolean flag on the shared DruidAbstractDataSource. Once one connection is closed by a different thread, this flag becomes true for ALL connections in the pool. The flag is never reset to false. This means a single cross-thread close permanently changes the behavior of the entire datasource, enabling the slower synchronous close path for all subsequent connections even when the same thread is closing them.
suspicions.suspected_bug: setAsyncCloseConnectionEnable(true) is a permanent side effect from a single cross-thread close; all subsequent connections will use sync close path even when closed by the same thread, causing unnecessary performance degradation

suspicions.observation: In RandomDataSourceSelector.removeBlackList() at line 204-217, when `blacklist.size() >= dataSourceMap.size()`, it returns ALL data sources (`dataSourceSet = dataSourceMap.values()`), INCLUDING the blacklisted ones. This means when the blacklist threshold is reached and all available sources are blacklisted, the method falls back to returning even the blacklisted data sources. While this might be intentional as a fallback, it violates the blacklist contract - callers should not receive blacklisted sources.
suspicions.suspected_bug: When all data sources are blacklisted, removeBlackList returns them anyway, effectively bypassing the blacklist mechanism and routing traffic to known-bad data sources

suspicions.observation: In JtdsXAResource.isSameRM() at line 90, the call `((JtdsXAResource) xares).getRmHost().equals(this.rmHost)` can throw NullPointerException. If the other XAResource's `rmHost` is null (because the reflection-based `getRmHost` method lookup or invocation failed in the constructor), calling `.equals()` on null will throw NPE.
suspicions.suspected_bug: isSameRM() throws NullPointerException when the other JtdsXAResource's rmHost field is null due to failed reflection initialization

suspicions.observation: In SQLJSONValueExpr.equals() at line 10, the method always returns `false` without checking if `this == o`. Even when comparing an instance to itself, it returns false. This violates the Java Object contract (reflexivity: x.equals(x) must be true). The hashCode() method always returns 0, which violates the equals/hashCode contract - all instances will have the same hash code.
suspicions.suspected_bug: SQLJSONValueExpr.equals() always returns false (violating reflexivity: x.equals(x) == false), and hashCode() always returns 0, breaking collection semantics when used in HashMap/HashSet

suspicions.observation: In RandomDataSourceValidateThread.checkAllDataSources() at lines 201-205, the error count increment is a non-atomic compound action: `if (!errorCounts.containsKey(name)) { errorCounts.put(name, 0); } int count = errorCounts.get(name); errorCounts.put(name, count + 1);` Multiple validation threads executing concurrently can read the same count value and both write count+1, losing one increment. The error count could be stuck below the threshold, delaying or preventing a legitimately faulty data source from being blacklisted.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Race condition in errorCounts increment: concurrent validation threads lose increments, causing undercounted errors and delayed/wrong blacklist decisions

suspicions.observation: In RandomDataSourceSelector.removeBusyDataSource() at line 226, the condition `busyDataSourceSet.size() < dataSourceSet.size()` means that if ALL data sources are busy, none are removed from the selection set. The guard prevents removing all data sources, but then the caller getRandomDataSource will still try to use these busy data sources that have poolingCount <= 0.
suspicions.suspected_bug: When all data sources are busy (poolingCount <= 0), removeBusyDataSource doesn't remove any of them, so getConnection will still route to busy data sources that have no available connections

bugs.observation: In DruidDataSource.tryGetConnection() at line 283-287, it checks `if (poolingCount == 0) return null;` then calls `return getConnection();`. The `getConnection()` method can block (up to maxWait milliseconds) waiting for connections. The TOCTOU race: between checking poolingCount==0 and calling getConnection(), another thread might have taken the last pooled connection, causing this method to block indefinitely (up to maxWait) when the caller expects a non-blocking behavior.
bugs.suspected_bug: tryGetConnection() violates its non-blocking contract - it can block even when poolingCount was 0, because getConnection() will create new connections or wait for existing ones
